rule_name: Subordinate Instead of Chaining With "And" / "Then"
quote: and it is an hour a day, every day, and the sheet says it runs to the end
why: three unequal clauses (when it starts, its frequency, its duration) are coordinated with flat "and" instead of a hierarchy that shows which fact matters most
suggestion: Self defense starts in September, an hour a day, every day; the sheet says it runs to the end of the year.

rule_name: Dialogue Formatting and Typography
quote: "Ten's a lot." Sam says.
why: a period splits the tag from the line it belongs to, inconsistent with the comma-tag convention the same chapter uses elsewhere (e.g. line 57's "'She says a lot of things,' Sam says")
suggestion: "Ten's a lot," Sam says.

rule_name: The "Nobody" Construction, Don't Normalise by Reporting an Absent Reaction
quote: nobody says anything for a while
why: reports a collective absence of reaction as evidence of the moment's weight rather than giving one character's actual small reaction
suggestion: Ruth says nothing, one arm still over her eyes.

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: for a while
why: "for a while" is the exact universal duration marker the rule bans, used here regardless of what kind of moment is being timed
suggestion: sit on the floor in the corridor outside, not talking

rule_name: Put the Comedy Straight After the Violence
quote: nobody says anything for a while
why: this inserts a beat of stillness right after the sparring (Sam's bloody nose) and before Sam's deflecting joke arrives several lines later, when the rule calls for the joke to land on the next line with no stillness first
suggestion: cut the stillness beat and let Sam's line follow immediately: "...that nobody did on purpose. 'She says a lot of things,' Sam says, into his sleeve."

rule_name: Filtering, Cut "She Sees / Hears / Notices / Knows"
quote: knows which two seconds of it she wasted
why: routes Chloe's own self-assessment through the filter verb "knows" instead of stating the wasted seconds directly
suggestion: Chloe is on eleven seconds by June, and two of them she wasted.

rule_name: STYLE_RULES section 8: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Anaphora / three-beat lists)
quote: For two weeks everybody is bad at it. Everybody knows why they are bad at it, because the ball goes four times faster than a dart and there is a wall of paint behind the target to prove it. Nobody has any idea what to do about it, including Bell, who is not saying.
why: three successive totalizing clauses ("everybody is bad" / "Everybody knows why" / "Nobody has any idea") form the banned anaphoric three-beat pattern instead of one collapsed statement
suggestion: For two weeks everybody is bad at it, because the ball goes four times faster than a dart and there's a wall of paint behind the target to prove it, and Bell isn't saying what to do about it.

rule_name: Paragraph Breaks, Keep One Beat in One Paragraph
quote: Chloe stops.
why: the action that leads directly into Chloe's interruption is set as its own paragraph, separated from the dialogue it triggers, splitting one beat into two
suggestion: Merge the beats: "Chloe stops. 'Wait. That's it. We're reacting.'"

rule_name: Vague Abstractions, Replace "Something," "Nothing," "The Whole Thing"
quote: says something about luck
why: "something" stands in for an actual line the boy could have said, flattening a specific moment into a gray placeholder
suggestion: "Lucky," the boy she is paired with says.

rule_name: Filtering, Cut "She Sees / Hears / Notices / Knows"
quote: Chloe knows the afternoon it happens
why: routes the fact about Kavi through the filter verb "knows" instead of rendering the stimulus (his changed number, his silent exit) directly
suggestion: His number goes from three to ten inside one hour, and he walks out without saying a word to anybody.

rule_name: STYLE_RULES section 8: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Symmetry / mirrored halves)
quote: The fire alarm going, and the fire alarm being the point of it.
why: the two halves repeat "the fire alarm" in matching grammatical shape, restating rather than adding information
suggestion: The fire alarm going, with nobody warned it's the drill this time.

rule_name: STYLE_RULES section 8: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Interiority of non-POV characters)
quote: before she has seen anybody
why: attributes an internal perceptual state (what she has or hasn't seen) to an unnamed non-POV student, information Chloe could not actually have
suggestion: One of the twelve is off her feet before she turns around.

rule_name: Keep Narrative Tense Consistent Unless the Break Is Signalled
quote: Russian started in September
why: drops into simple past while every parallel "X starts in [month]" sentence in this same chapter (self defense, the 10v1, paintball, algebra) is present tense, with no signalled break
suggestion: Russian starts in September

rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
quote: She is unusually good at hearing a thing once and writing it down.
why: a bare verdict on her ability, stated before the concrete evidence (eight bars caught whole against the next girl's four notes) that should be doing the work alone
suggestion: cut the sentence and let the anecdote carry it: "She finds that out in the third week, when he plays eight bars and she gets the whole of it while the girl next to her gets four notes."

rule_name: Inhabit the Subject, and Give the Reader One Line of It
quote: The factory goes, then the people who knew how to run it get other jobs, and then in fifteen years they're sixty and there's nobody left who's ever done it.
why: delivers a paragraph-length chain of the actual economic argument rather than the single characterizing line the rule calls for, reading closer to the syllabus than to a kid talking
suggestion: keep the first line ("There are industries you have to still have in twenty years even if somebody else is cheaper today") and cut the rest of the chain, letting her father's next question pull out only what's needed

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: for a second
why: "for a second" is used here as the generic universal duration marker the rule specifically bans rather than a real, specific beat
suggestion: Her father considers his plate.

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: and that is the end of tariffs
why: matches the banned reflexive scene-closer "and that's the end of it" almost verbatim, wrapping up the scene with filler instead of the last concrete image
suggestion: cut the closer and end on the image: "...and her aunt wants to know who is having cream."

rule_name: Vague Abstractions, Replace "Something," "Nothing," "The Whole Thing"
quote: does a small thing with his eyebrows
why: "a small thing" is a vague placeholder standing in for an actual, nameable expression
suggestion: and lifts one eyebrow at her

rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
quote: and it is good
why: a bare quality verdict with no supporting fact in the sentence, and the scene that follows (a note flagging something wrong on page six) doesn't confirm it either
suggestion: ...with eleven minutes to go, and she doesn't change a word before she hands it in.

rule_name: Banned Constructions, Assert Nothing, Show the Substance
quote: comes out good again
why: a second bare quality verdict ("good") standing in place of a specific fact that would let the reader reach the same conclusion
suggestion: but it comes out three pages longer than anything she's written before

rule_name: Paragraph Breaks, Keep One Beat in One Paragraph
quote: sits there with her fork for a second
why: the action beat that leads directly into Chloe's answer is set off in its own paragraph, splitting one continuous beat into two isolated ones
suggestion: Merge the beats: "...and then sits there with her fork for a second. 'He hasn't changed one single thing about any of it...'"

rule_name: Crutch Phrases That Have Stopped Meaning Anything
quote: for a second
why: another instance of "for a second" used as a generic, interchangeable duration marker rather than a real beat
suggestion: turns her fork over once before answering

rule_name: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Em dashes)
quote: g to get a hand there and by the time we—"
why: em dash; the ban applies everywhere, dialogue included
suggestion: replace with a comma or a short hyphen

rule_name: Automatic-fail narrator constructions (Em dashes)
quote: He points the fork at her. "That's the b—"
why: em dash; the ban applies everywhere, dialogue included
suggestion: replace with a comma or a short hyphen
